::: {.solutions}

**24 questions.** Suggested time: **100 minutes**, no calculator.

Every question comes from a TMUA past paper or a TMUA-style mock, and its source is shown beside the question number. None of
them appears in the S3 class questions.

For every question the routine is the same: **find the condition and the target, then write the arrow.** Sufficient is
condition $\Rightarrow$ target, and necessary is target $\Rightarrow$ condition. Where you can, work out the exact condition
first, then compare the options with it.

| Section | What it covers | Questions |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Read the verdict** | two statements or a list of conditions; test each arrow | 1–7 |
| **B — Find the exact condition** | work out exactly when it holds, then compare the options | 8–12 |
| **C — Polynomials, derivatives and integrals** | what a condition on $f$ forces, and what it does not | 13–20 |
| **D — Symmetry and transformations** | turning a graph condition into one exact equation | 21–24 |

---

::: {.question}

> $(*)$: $ab$ is divisible by $n$

The condition "either $a$ or $b$ is divisible by $n$" is:

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** necessary but not sufficient for $(*)$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** sufficient but not necessary for $(*)$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** necessary and sufficient for $(*)$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** not necessary and not sufficient for $(*)$
:::

## Question 3 &nbsp;<span style="font-size:0.72em;color:#8a8a8a;font-weight:400">2021 · P2 Q3</span>

::: {.question}
A student is chosen at random from a class. Each student is equally likely to be chosen.

Which of the following conditions is/are **necessary** for the probability that the student wears glasses to equal

&nbsp;&nbsp;**I** &nbsp; Exactly $11$ students in the class do not wear glasses.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**II** &nbsp; The number of students in the class is divisible by $3$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**III** &nbsp; The class contains $30$ students, and $8$ of them wear glasses.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** none of them

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** I only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** II only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** III only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** I and II only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**F** I and III only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**G** II and III only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**H** I, II and III
:::

A TMUA question asks candidates to identify which one of the conditions below is a **sufficient but not necessary**
condition for some statement $P$, concerning a real number $x$, to hold.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $\dfrac b2=\sqrt{\dfrac{a^{2}+b^{2}}{4}-c}$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** $-\dfrac a2=\sqrt{\dfrac{a^{2}+b^{2}}{4}-c}$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**F** $-\dfrac b2=\sqrt{\dfrac{a^{2}+b^{2}}{4}-c}$

## Question 11 &nbsp;<span style="font-size:0.72em;color:#8a8a8a;font-weight:400">2020 · P2 Q14</span>

::: {.question}
An arithmetic sequence $T$ has first term $a$ and common difference $d$, where $a$ and $d$ are non-zero integers.

Property $P$ is:

> For some positive integer $m$, the sum of the first $m$ terms of the sequence is equal to the sum of the first $2m$ terms
> of the sequence.

For example, when $a=11$ and $d=-2$, the sequence $T$ has property $P$, because

$$11+9+7+5=11+9+7+5+3+1+(-1)+(-3)$$

i.e. the sum of the first $4$ terms equals the sum of the first $8$ terms.

Which of the following statements is/are true?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**I** &nbsp; For $T$ to have property $P$, it is sufficient that $ad<0$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**II** &nbsp; For $T$ to have property $P$, it is necessary that $d$ is even.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** neither of them

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** I only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** II only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** I and II
:::

::: {.workspace style="min-height:7cm"}
Working
:::

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** Only 4.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**F** Only 1 and 2.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**G** Only 1 and 3.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**H** Only 1 and 4.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**I** Only 2 and 3.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**J** Only 2 and 4.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** none of them

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** I only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** II only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** III only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** I and II only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**F** I and III only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**G** II and III only

&nbsp;&nbsp;**H** I, II and III

&nbsp;&nbsp;**II** &nbsp; $\mathrm f(2a-x)=\mathrm f(x)$ for all real $x$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**III** &nbsp; $\mathrm f(a-x)=\mathrm f(x)$ for all real $x$.

Which of these conditions is/are **necessary and sufficient** for the graph of $y=\mathrm f(x)$ to have reflection symmetry
in the line $x=a$?

| | Condition I is | Condition II is | Condition III is |
|---|---|---|---|
| | necessary and sufficient | necessary and sufficient | necessary and sufficient |
| **A** | yes | yes | yes |
| **B** | yes | yes | no |
| **C** | yes | no | yes |
| **D** | yes | no | no |
| **E** | no | yes | yes |
| **F** | no | yes | no |
| **G** | no | no | yes |
| **H** | no | no | no |
:::

## Question 22 &nbsp;<span style="font-size:0.72em;color:#8a8a8a;font-weight:400">2019 · P2 Q20</span>

::: {.question}
When the graph of the function $y=\mathrm f(x)$, defined on the real numbers, is reflected in the $y$-axis and then translated by
$2$ units in the negative $x$-direction, the result is the graph of the function $y=\mathrm g(x)$.

When the graph of the same function $y=\mathrm f(x)$ is translated by $2$ units in the negative $x$-direction and then reflected in
the $y$-axis, the result is the graph of the function $y=\mathrm h(x)$.

Which one of the following conditions on $y=\mathrm f(x)$ is **necessary and sufficient** for the functions $\mathrm g(x)$ and
$\mathrm h(x)$ to be identical?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $\mathrm f(x)=\mathrm f(x+2)$ for all $x$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $\mathrm f(x)=\mathrm f(x+4)$ for all $x$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** $\mathrm f(x)=\mathrm f(x+8)$ for all $x$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $\mathrm f(x)=\mathrm f(-x)$ for all $x$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** $\mathrm f(x)=\mathrm f(2-x)$ for all $x$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**F** $\mathrm f(x)=\mathrm f(4-x)$ for all $x$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**G** $\mathrm f(x)=\mathrm f(8-x)$ for all $x$
:::

## Question 23 &nbsp;<span style="font-size:0.72em;color:#8a8a8a;font-weight:400">JZ Maths Mock C · P2 Q16</span>

::: {.question}
Three transformations of the plane are defined as follows. $R$ is the reflection in the $y$-axis. $T$ is the translation by $4$
units in the positive $x$-direction. $S$ is the horizontal stretch with scale factor $2$ parallel to the $x$-axis, fixing the
$y$-axis.

Let $y=f(x)$ be a function defined on the real numbers.

When the graph of $y=f(x)$ is transformed by applying $R$, then $T$, then $S$ in that order, the result is the graph of
$y=g(x)$.

When the graph of the same function $y=f(x)$ is transformed by applying $S$, then $T$, then $R$ in that order, the result is
the graph of $y=h(x)$.

Which one of the following conditions on $y=f(x)$ is **necessary and sufficient** for the functions $g(x)$ and $h(x)$ to be
identical?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $f(x)=f(x+3)$ for all $x$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $f(x)=f(x+4)$ for all $x$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** $f(x)=f(x+6)$ for all $x$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $f(x)=f(x+12)$ for all $x$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** $f(x)=f(-x)$ for all $x$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**F** $f(x)=f(6-x)$ for all $x$
:::

When the graph of $y=f(x)$ is reflected in the $y$-axis and then stretched in the $x$-direction by a factor of $\tfrac12$, the

When the graph of $y=f(x)$ is stretched in the $x$-direction by a factor of $\tfrac12$ and then translated by $1$ unit in the

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $f(0)=f(2)$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $f(x)=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{10}\cos(\pi kx)$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** $f(x)=f(1-x)$ for all $x$

&nbsp;&nbsp;**F** $f(x)=\cos(\pi x)+\sin(\pi x)$
